Commuters who usually rely on passenger jeepneys resort to tricycles amid a transport strike that leaves several routes without jeepney operations in Nagtahan, Manila on Wednesday, April 15.

Transport groups Manibela and PISTON staged a nationwide strike from April 15 to 17 in protest of rising fuel prices and other sectoral concerns.

The disruption forced thousands of daily passengers to seek alternative modes of transport, resulting in longer travel times and higher fares.

📷: Mark Balmores | MB

🚨 **BREAKING: VP Sara Duterte Drops Fiery Statement – And It's Pure Fire!** 🔥

Mga kababayan, just when you thought the "mini-trial" circus couldn't get any more desperate... VP Sara Z. Duterte just released her official statement today (April 15, 2026) and it's an absolute masterclass in clapping back with facts, dignity, and zero filter. 👏

Of all the wild accusations thrown during the House Committee on Justice hearing yesterday (April 14), the one that clearly got under her skin was this:

> “Of all the lies thrown during the Committee on Justice ‘mini trial’ on April 14, the one I personally take issue with is the claim, made by a **bar flunker and kidnapping suspect**, that I needed someone to help me get through law school.” 😤

VP Sara didn't hold back. She went straight to the heart of the smear:

> “I completed my studies on my own terms. I placed a higher premium on living a well-rounded life rather than pursuing academic excellence. I never asked any professor for special accommodation for my grades because the bare minimum was easy enough to meet. I was never the subject of any complaint for rudeness or violence against other students at SSC-R College of Law.” 💪

Then the mic drop on her actual record:

> “I graduated in May 2005 and took the Bar Exam in September of the same year—something that had not been done before at SSC-R College of Law until my time. The exam that year was relatively difficult. I passed the Bar on my first attempt with a GWA of 80, five points above the minimum.” 📚✅

I'm genuinely amazed at how calmly and powerfully she dismantled the hearsay from a questionable witness while keeping the focus on truth and results. 😲

She even called out the bigger picture:

> “Madriga[ga] and his cohorts in the House of Representatives do not come close to my capacity to achieve results with very little effort because they cannot even weave a believable lie, much less follow the rule of law.” 

And closed with a strong reminder about priorities in these tough times.

This statement is not just a defense — it's a reminder of why so many Filipinos admire her straightforward style. No drama, no victim card, just facts and strength. 🇵🇭

Truth is breaking through the noise once again. Respect, VP Sara! 🙌

#SaraDuterte #VPSara #TruthOverLies #Philippines

@indaysara

ADVISORY

Please be informed that recent air quality monitoring in Manila indicates increased air pollution levels associated with the ongoing fire incident at the Navotas Sanitary Landfill. This pollution contains small particulate matter (PM2.5) that can enter the lungs and cause respiratory irritation, especially among vulnerable groups such as elderlies, children, infants, pregnant women, and individuals with pre-existing heart or lung conditions.

The public is advised to wear N95 or KN95 masks when outdoors. If unavailable, double surgical masks or a clean, damp cloth may be used as temporary alternatives. Limit outdoor activities and stay indoors whenever possible. Keep doors and windows closed and seal gaps with damp cloths.

Stay hydrated and ensure that medications for respiratory conditions are readily available. Seek immediate medical attention for any signs of breathing difficulty or related symptoms.

The University of the Philippines Manila strongly encourages all students, faculty, and employees to adhere to these precautions to reduce health risks associated with poor air quality.

Source: Department of Health and Manila Public Information Office

#SciFeature 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗛𝗬𝗣𝗘 𝗢𝗡 “𝗦𝗨𝗣𝗘𝗥 𝗧𝗬𝗣𝗛𝗢𝗢𝗡 𝗖𝗔𝗟𝗢𝗬” 𝗜𝗦 𝗔 𝗥𝗘𝗠𝗜𝗡𝗗𝗘𝗥 𝗧𝗢 𝗕𝗘 𝗠𝗢𝗥𝗘 𝗖𝗔𝗥𝗘𝗙𝗨𝗟 𝗜𝗡 𝗥𝗘𝗣𝗢𝗥𝗧𝗜𝗡𝗚 𝗟𝗢𝗡𝗚-𝗥𝗔𝗡𝗚𝗘 𝗙𝗢𝗥𝗘𝗖𝗔𝗦𝗧𝗦 

When tropical cyclone #Sinlaku was still forming over a week ago, several weather pages and personalities in the Philippines quickly hyped its possible entry into the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR), even labeling it a potential “Super Typhoon Caloy.”

But in the end, it never entered PAR and eventually veered away, leaving behind unnecessary panic, confusion, and frustration.

Much of the online buzz leaned heavily on worst-case scenarios that drive engagement, rather than clearly explaining the uncertainties of long-range forecasts. Day after day, headlines focused on possible PAR entry, even going as far as pre-naming it “#Caloy”, as if its arrival was already certain. 

Meanwhile, far less attention was given to a crucial question: 𝗪𝗶𝗹𝗹 𝗶𝘁 𝗮𝗰𝘁𝘂𝗮𝗹𝗹𝘆 𝗮𝗳𝗳𝗲𝗰𝘁 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗣𝗵𝗶𝗹𝗶𝗽𝗽𝗶𝗻𝗲𝘀 𝗮𝘁 𝗮𝗹𝗹?

So what can we learn from this? 

[𝟭] 𝗦𝗵𝗶𝗳𝘁 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗳𝗼𝗰𝘂𝘀 𝗳𝗿𝗼𝗺 “𝗪𝗶𝗹𝗹 𝗶𝘁 𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗿 𝗣𝗔𝗥?” 𝘁𝗼 “𝗪𝗶𝗹𝗹 𝗶𝘁 𝗮𝗳𝗳𝗲𝗰𝘁 𝘂𝘀?”

PAR entry does not automatically mean landfall or significant impacts. Communicating potential effects—rainfall, winds, flooding—is far more meaningful than simply tracking boundaries.

[𝟮] 𝗥𝗲𝘀𝗽𝗲𝗰𝘁 𝘂𝗻𝗰𝗲𝗿𝘁𝗮𝗶𝗻𝘁𝘆, 𝗲𝘀𝗽𝗲𝗰𝗶𝗮𝗹𝗹𝘆 𝗶𝗻 𝗹𝗼𝗻𝗴-𝗿𝗮𝗻𝗴𝗲 𝗳𝗼𝗿𝗲𝗰𝗮𝘀𝘁𝘀.

Forecast models are tools, not guarantees. Avoid favoring the most alarming scenario just because it drives engagement. Present multiple possibilities and make uncertainty clear.

[𝟯] 𝗔𝘃𝗼𝗶𝗱 𝗽𝗿𝗲-𝗻𝗮𝗺𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗿𝗺𝘀.

Assigning a local name prematurely can create a false sense of certainty. If the system never enters PAR, it can erode public confidence over time.

Every weather and hazard-related post we share carries real-world consequences. The information we put out shapes how people prepare, respond, and protect themselves. It can save lives, but careless messaging can just as easily put them at risk. 

𝗦𝗰𝗶𝗲𝗻𝗰𝗲𝗞𝗼𝗻𝗲𝗸 
15 April 2026

data.english_translation: #SciFeature 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗛𝗬𝗣𝗘 𝗢𝗡 “𝗦𝗨𝗣𝗘𝗥 𝗧𝗬𝗣𝗛𝗢𝗢𝗡 𝗖𝗔𝗟𝗢𝗬” 𝗜𝗦 𝗔 𝗥𝗘𝗠𝗜𝗡𝗗𝗘𝗥 𝗧𝗢 𝗕𝗘 𝗠𝗢𝗥𝗘 𝗖𝗔𝗥𝗘𝗙𝗨𝗟 𝗜𝗡 𝗥𝗘𝗣𝗢𝗥𝗧𝗜𝗡𝗚 𝗟𝗢𝗡𝗚-𝗥𝗔𝗡𝗚𝗘 𝗙𝗢𝗥𝗘𝗖𝗔𝗦𝗧𝗦 When tropical cyclone #Sinlaku was still forming over a week ago, several weather pages and personalities in the Philippines quickly hyped its possible entry into the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR), even labeling it a potential “Super Typhoon Caloy.” But in the end, it never entered PAR and eventually veered away, leaving behind unnecessary panic, confusion, and frustration. Much of the online buzz leaned heavily on worst-case scenarios that drive engagement, rather than clearly explaining the uncertainties of long-range forecasts. Day after day, headlines focused on possible PAR entry, even going as far as pre-naming it “#Caloy”, as if its arrival was already certain. Meanwhile, far less attention was given to a crucial question: 𝗪𝗶𝗹𝗹 𝗶𝘁 𝗮𝗰𝘁𝘂𝗮𝗹𝗹𝘆 𝗮𝗳𝗳𝗲𝗰𝘁 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗣𝗵𝗶𝗹𝗶𝗽𝗽𝗶𝗻𝗲𝘀 𝗮𝘁 𝗮𝗹𝗹? So what can we learn from this? [𝟭] 𝗦𝗵𝗶𝗳𝘁 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗳𝗼𝗰𝘂𝘀 𝗳𝗿𝗼𝗺 “𝗪𝗶𝗹𝗹 𝗶𝘁 𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗿 𝗣𝗔𝗥?” 𝘁𝗼 “𝗪𝗶𝗹𝗹 𝗶𝘁 𝗮𝗳𝗳𝗲𝗰𝘁 𝘂𝘀?” PAR entry does not automatically mean landfall or significant impacts. Communicating potential effects—rainfall, winds, flooding—is far more meaningful than simply tracking boundaries. [𝟮] 𝗥𝗲𝘀𝗽𝗲𝗰𝘁 𝘂𝗻𝗰𝗲𝗿𝘁𝗮𝗶𝗻𝘁𝘆, 𝗲𝘀𝗽𝗲𝗰𝗶𝗮𝗹𝗹𝘆 𝗶𝗻 𝗹𝗼𝗻𝗴-𝗿𝗮𝗻𝗴𝗲 𝗳𝗼𝗿𝗲𝗰𝗮𝘀𝘁𝘀. Forecast models are tools, not guarantees. Avoid favoring the most alarming scenario just because it drives engagement. Present multiple possibilities and make uncertainty clear. [𝟯] 𝗔𝘃𝗼𝗶𝗱 𝗽𝗿𝗲-𝗻𝗮𝗺𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗿𝗺𝘀. Assigning a local name prematurely can create a false sense of certainty. If the system never enters PAR, it can erode public confidence over time. Every weather and hazard-related post we share carries real-world consequences. The information we put out shapes how people prepare, respond, and protect themselves. It can save lives, but careless messaging can just as easily put them at risk. 𝗦𝗰𝗶𝗲𝗻𝗰𝗲𝗞𝗼𝗻𝗲𝗸 15 April 2026

Naka-activate na ang MMDA Emergency Operations Center (EOC) sa unang araw ng tigil-pasada na isinasagawa ng ilang transport groups sa pangunguna ng Manibela at Piston.

Nai-report sa EOC ang ilang rally ng mga grupo sa Quezon City, Pasay City, Paranaque City ngayong umaga para iprotesta ang nararanasang krisis ng transport sector sa gitna ng patuloy na pagtaas ng presyo ng langis. Wala pang stranded na pasahero ang nai-report.

Pinangunahan ni MMDA Deputy Chairman Usec. Frisco San Juan Jr. ang pagmo-monitor ng sitwasyon sa EDSA at iba pang pangunahing lansangan, sa direktiba ni MMDA Chairman Atty. Don Artes.

Naka-preposition at standby naman ang mga behikulo na magsasakay ng mga pasahero na maaaring maaapektuhan ng transport strike. Idedeploy lamang ang mga sasakyan kung kinakailangan.
 #mmda #mmdaatyourservice
